Wording, code, title and band are right. (1) Scope of a condition: the statement puts the condition of doing it together with other people at the very end, after its second half (coming up with solutions); it does not attach it to the first half (picking the problem out and discussing it). The Summary opens with 'works together with other people on a problem' and puts all three steps under it, and Limits states it as settled ('The child does this with others, not alone'). The wide reading is possible, but the wording does not settle it; say so in Limits, as the Limits of 5.C.1 does for its support condition. (2) The Summary narrows the first verb to speech ('they say what the problem is'); the statement's first verb is one of picking out.

Wording, code, title and band are right, and the Summary keeps the three sentences apart. Limits: 'the statement does not mention roads, strangers or screens' is said of the whole statement, but only its middle sentence (the describing one) is limited to bodily danger and to the home and the place of learning. The first sentence (the reason for rules of safety) and the last (showing safe conduct) name no setting and no kind of safety, so road rules fall inside their general terms; the record's own In a child's hands uses a rule at a pool for the first sentence. A designer would read the Limits sentence as putting road safety outside this statement. Fix: attach the limit to the describing sentence only and say that the other two sentences set no setting.

The Summary gives the statement's first element an object it does not have: "reads situations more correctly". The statement says only that what the child perceives becomes more accurate, and not of what; under this competency (awareness of oneself) the child's view of themselves is meant at least as much as their reading of a situation, and the Summary leaves it out. The Summary also renders the ideas the child stays open to as "ideas unlike their own": the statement gives those ideas two qualities, and the first of them (that they are new to the child) is dropped. Fix: say that the child perceives more accurately, with no object, and keep both qualities. Not a near copy. Wording and code are in order.
